geometry.locator: The HAWC Gamma-Ray Observatory: Design, Calibration, and Operation, site-description section
geometry.note: 'verified': representation is 'surveyed' from a rank<=10 (design_report) source.
geometry.quote: The geographical latitude of the site is 18.99 ... The geographical longitude of the HAWC site, 97.31 W.

method: Coordinate taken directly from the HAWC design/operation paper's own stated site latitude and longitude (18.99 N, 97.31 W), fetched via a text-extraction proxy (r.jina.ai) after WebFetch could not parse the paper's PDF binary directly. accuracy_m 600 covers the two-decimal-degree rounding (+-0.005 degrees ~ 550 m at this latitude). This is a tighter, more directly relevant coordinate than the site record's current one (a Nominatim geocode of the Sierra Negra peak, precision_m 3000) -- reported as a site coordinate correction candidate in the worklog. The array's own footprint (300 tanks, ~20,000-22,500 m2, 'placed in joint pairs of rows' on a platform levelled from an 8% to a 1% slope) has no stated overall outline shape (circular/hexagonal/irregular) in the fetched text, so it is not drawn as a polygon this session.
name: HAWC array (reference point)
notes: 300-tank footprint (~20,000-22,500 m2) has no sourced overall outline shape this session; drawn as a point only. Backlog: a HAWC layout diagram or GIS file with tank-by-tank or corner coordinates.

summary.plain: The HAWC water-Cherenkov gamma-ray observatory on the Sierra Negra volcano, Mexico, shown here as a single reference point at the array's own published coordinate.
